findings.title: Public findMany() method removed without migrating or even checking callers
findings.body: The PR deletes the service's only data-access method, `findMany(findManyArgs)`, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which just returns a raw SQL fragment. It also changes the constructor's accepted options type from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the new `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`. No other files are changed in this PR, so any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService` (router, handler, repository, or an interface the class implements) that calls `.findMany(...)` will fail to compile, and consumers now have to hand-write `$queryRaw` queries themselves. Before merging, verify every caller of this service has been migrated (or keep a `findMany` that composes the raw query internally); if callers are migrated in a stacked PR, that dependency should be explicit, otherwise this is a breaking change.

findings.title: Authorization/filter SQL fragments are returned unparenthesized, so ANDing extra predicates silently changes semantics
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` for team/org scope returns a top-level `OR` expression like `("teamId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)` with no outer parentheses, and `getBaseConditions()` returns that auth fragment bare whenever there are no filters (`return authConditions`). Likewise `getFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` unwrapped. The old object-notation API merged conditions via Prisma `AND` arrays, so callers could safely add their own predicates; with the new raw-SQL API, any caller that writes `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ...` (the natural way to add date-range filtering in insights) gets `A OR B AND ...` which parses as `A OR (B AND ...)`, silently broadening the result set beyond the authorized scope — a potential data-exposure bug. Wrap the final reduced auth and filter expressions in parentheses (e.g. `Prisma.sql`(${combined})``) so the fragments are safely composable.

findings.title: Caching tests for authorization and filter conditions deleted while the caching code remains
findings.body: The PR removes the entire "Caching" describe block ("should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") from the integration tests. The service still implements and relies on that behavior via `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` in `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()`. Rather than updating the two assertions to the new `Prisma.sql` format (they would only have needed the expected value changed, since the second call returning the cached object is format-agnostic), the coverage was dropped entirely, leaving the memoization logic untested. Restore equivalent tests asserting that a second call returns the identical cached `Prisma.Sql` instance.
